note: no grid served; token 2233 chars; aria-checked=true
lesson: human-paced trusted click (780ms observed) passes WITHOUT provoking a grid; machine-speed 8ms batched input PROVOKED the grid. Never batch observed input.

note: trusted click at iframe.x+24, iframe.y+h/2; token 794 chars
lesson: checkbox sits behind closed shadow root -> cross-origin iframe. Do NOT grab it: DOM.getDocument pierce:true finds the challenge iframe, DOM.getBoxModel gives the box, trusted click on the glass does the rest.

note: red-circle grid with similar reds/oranges: returned 2,7,11,12,14,16 vs truth 2,7,11
lesson: gemma4:31b over-includes on subtle colour discrimination (3 false positives). Accurate model (kimi-k2.7-code) is the default rung V1; gemma4:31b is rung V2, escalate only when speed-bound AND high-contrast. A wrong grid answer costs a round + reset, so it is slower than any model latency.

LIVE GRID SOLVED, first attempt. gemma4:31b LEADS the vision ladder: 881-1073ms on real photographic tiles vs kimi-k2.7-code 15620ms AND TRUNCATED (no ANSWER sentinel). Earlier 'gemma4 is inaccurate' verdict came from an artificial colour-discrimination grid and does NOT hold for real reCAPTCHA tiles. Round prompts VARY within one challenge (buses 4x4 -> cars 3x3): always re-read prompt + tile count each round, never assume 16.

note: 15620ms, finish_reason truncated, no ANSWER sentinel emitted
lesson: A truncating reasoning model returns mid-sentence text. NEVER fall back to parsing the last line: the old fallback silently produced tile numbers [2,3,4] from the sentence '...Wheels at 65'. Require the ANSWER sentinel or treat the look as FAILED and escalate.

CORRECTION to an earlier lesson: the 'gemma4 is inaccurate / use kimi first' conclusion is WITHDRAWN. It was based on ONE artificial grid of similar reds/oranges that does not represent real tiles. Real-grid evidence (buses + cars, solved) shows gemma4:31b 881-1073ms vs kimi-k2.7-code 15620ms truncated. gemma4 leads V1. Re-test on substance/containers (bicycles, traffic lights, crosswalks) when they appear, and let the ledger decide, not the synthetic case.

note: STRICT prompt + reasoning_effort=low: 15955ms, 29-char reply, sentinel emitted, 3/3 truth hit
lesson: PROMPT ENGINEERING for kimi-k2.7-code: (1) The VERBOSE prompt makes it worse - 26.7s and finish_reason=length with NO sentinel (12k chars of reasoning). The STRICT prompt (task + 'Judge each tile once. No explanation, no restating. Final line exactly: ANSWER: <numbers or NONE>') gives a 29-char reply with a usable sentinel. Shortening the prompt SHORTENED the thinking. (2) NEVER put a real example answer in the prompt: a literal 'ANSWER: 2,7,11' was PARROTED back in 1.5s with no image consultation. Use an angle-bracket placeholder. (3) reasoning_effort IS accepted: low/medium/high all 9/9 correct at 15-17s, so the level buys no accuracy - use low for the small speed gain. (4) think=False does NOT stop thinking (still ~12k chars, 45s, truncated): there is no thinking-off switch. Control length via prompt + token budget. (5) raise max_tokens to 4000 - at 3000 a full trace leaves no room for the answer.

note: CLEAR grid: 3/3 hit, 0 FP on all 5 prompt variants; fastest with 'fewest' (716ms)
target: controlled grid: clear red-vs-orange + shape distractors
lesson: HARNESS BUG CORRECTED: an earlier 'models hedge wide' result was MY off-by-one - I passed 1-based tile numbers into a 0-based drawing index, planting shapes one tile late. Both models had answered correctly. LESSON: always verify planted ground truth with an independent pixel audit before scoring the model. On a CLEAR discrimination task both gemma and kimi are already perfectly discriminative (0 FP); no prompt engineering needed.

note: baseline/define/binary = 2 FP; 'fewest' and 'distractor' framing = 1 FP (716-818ms, still 3/3)
target: controlled grid: blood-red vs crimson triangles (deliberately ambiguous)
lesson: PROMPT ENGINEERING DOES HELP, MODESTLY: on a genuinely ambiguous grid, 'Select the FEWEST tiles that unambiguously qualify. If unsure, leave it out. A wrong extra tile is worse than a missed tile' halved gemma4:31b false positives (2 FP -> 1 FP). It never reached 0 FP. Crucially NO prompt caused under-selection: hit stayed 3/3 in every one of the 20 test cells, so tightening is risk-free here - it only removed distractors.

note: 2 FP on ALL five prompt phrasings (baseline, define, binary, fewest, distractor)
target: controlled grid: blood-red vs crimson triangles
lesson: kimi-k2.7-code is IMMUNE to prompt phrasing on ambiguous colour discrimination: 2 false positives regardless of how the instruction is worded. Its reasoning trace drives the answer, not the instruction. Do not spend prompt budget tuning a reasoning model's discrimination - escalate or accept the hedge.

note: widget left untouched 80s, then human-paced click -> 9-tile 'bicycles' grid ARMED (not expired, no error)
lesson: IDLE-TIME TRAP IS REAL: leaving the v2 checkbox untouched for 80s then clicking ARMS A GRID, where immediate clicking passes with no grid. The widget itself does NOT time out (no error text, still clickable, anchor frame healthy) - but the delayed click is scored as low-confidence and escalates to the image challenge. Human-plausible pacing must include the CLICK ARRIVING PROMPTLY, not just human-shaped motion + pauses. An unexplained idle gap before the first interaction is itself a signal.

note: 9-tile 'bicycles' grid: gemma4:31b 765ms -> [1,3,4]; PASS 1 round; token 2297 chars
lesson: A 3x3 (9-tile) grid solved first try in one round. Grids armed by a delayed click are still solvable normally - the delay changes the CHALLENGE LEVEL, not the solvability. Re-read tile count every round: 16 (buses/cars earlier) and 9 (bicycles) both occur.

task: Select all squares with traffic lights

note: 16-tile 'traffic lights' solved FIRST ROUND: 843ms -> [6,9]; token 2340 chars
target: google.com/recaptcha/api2/demo, grid armed by delayed click
lesson: Traffic lights is one of the hardest reCAPTCHA classes (small, low-contrast, easily confused with car lights/reflectors) and gemma4:31b solved a 16-tile version in ONE round at 843ms, unassisted, no escalation. Strong evidence the V1-fast-rung-first ordering is right; the earlier 'gemma is sloppy' verdict was an artefact of my synthetic colour task, not real tiles.

note: 3-round chain: 'bicycles' 16-tile -> [12]; same challenge RE-SERVED -> [12] again (passed); then 'cars' 9-tile -> [1,5,8]; token 2297
lesson: reCAPTCHA sometimes RE-SERVES the identical prompt+tiles after an answer. The correct response is simply to answer again with the ledger-verified rung - the second identical answer was accepted. Do NOT treat a re-serve as a wrong answer and switch rungs; that would discard a correct answer. Distinguish 'same prompt, same tiles' (answer again) from 'new prompt' (fresh look).

note: BOTH arms armed a grid: continuous pointer motion during wait -> 16-tile traffic lights; completely idle -> 16-tile bicycles. A subsequent repeat armed 16-tile traffic lights again.
lesson: IDLE-vs-TIME HYPOTHESIS RESOLVED: it is NEITHER idleness NOR a timeout. The widget never expires (no error text, stays clickable, anchor frame healthy after 80s). Rather, ANY substantial delay before the first click escalates the challenge level to an image grid. Continuous pointer motion during the wait did not help - it still escalated. So the escalation is driven by the LATENCY BEFORE FIRST INTERACTION, not by absence of motion. Human pacing must include CLICKING PROMPTLY; plausible motion does not compensate for a late click.
Ported solver verified from the standalone repo: config-driven target, persistent CDP transport, no Hermes paths.

note: 3 rounds, prompt 'bicycles' repeated all 3 times, 9 tiles each; answers [2,5] -> [2,5,8] -> [2,5]; PASS token 2318
lesson: REFINES the re-serve lesson: the prompt AND tile count can repeat while the TILES THEMSELVES differ. Three rounds all said 'Select all images with bicycles' at 9 tiles, yet the model gave [2,5], then [2,5,8], then [2,5] - different answers are correct here because these are NEW images under a repeated prompt, not the same grid. So: re-read the screenshot and re-look EVERY round even when the prompt is unchanged. Do not cache a previous answer on prompt match.
Repo verified working from a clean git clone with env-only configuration.

Reproducibility confirmed: a clean git clone + pip install -r requirements.txt + env vars only (VISION_API_KEY, CDP_PORT) solved a live 2-round reCAPTCHA grid with gemma4:31b, no Hermes or other harness on the path. requirements.txt is sufficient.

CONFIRMS the pierce rung ON A LIVE CLOUDFLARE INTERSTITIAL (not just the peet.ws test page). DOM.getDocument{depth:-1,pierce:true} finds the challenge iframe while document.querySelectorAll('iframe') returns 0 (closed shadow root); DOM.getBoxModel gives the box in VIEWPORT coords (measured x:489.5 y:304 w:300 h:65) and Input.dispatchMouseEvent at (box.x+24, box.y+h/2) = (514,336) passes in ~2s, ONE attempt, on a cookieless profile. Supersedes the pixel-scan approach as the FIRST rung: no CSS->screen conversion (that mapping is ~20px off), no window activation, occlusion-proof. PIXEL FALLBACK REVEALED WHY IT IS STILL NEEDED: the pierce rung CANNOT see widget state (cross-origin iframe = no DOM, no pixels), so while Cloudflare serves the SPINNER variant it fires no-op clicks (3 wasted attempts observed). The pixel rung detects spinner-vs-checkbox and WAITS instead of clicking; measured auto-fallback solving at 66.8s after Rung A exhausted. Also measured: the pixel rung must search only the LEFT 30% of the widget box - the left edge is a 1px full-height bright BORDER and the Cloudflare LOGO is a ~35x24 blob at the RIGHT; a naive bright-square test clicked the logo and opened Cloudflare's privacy policy in a new tab.

LIVE 1337x GATE, full ladder. Four traps cost hours and each was indistinguishable from 'the solver is broken': (1) WINDOW OCCLUSION - two Chrome windows at (1920,24) and (1898,60) overlap almost entirely, so every root-window capture silently described the WRONG window; scope captures to one window's bounds. (2) window.screenX/screenY != X11 frame origin (~20px x / ~26px y measured) so CSS->screen mapping clicked (4410,623) when the checkbox was at (4432,598); prefer viewport-space CDP clicks which need no mapping at all. (3) MULTIPLE PAGE TARGETS - a mis-click opening a tab makes chrome-agent fail with 'Multiple page targets found', and a naive title read then returned an EMPTY title which PASSED a buggy 'solved' test that had solved nothing; close strays via raw HTTP /json/close/<targetId> (no websocket) and require a NON-EMPTY title. (4) the bright-square checkbox test matches the widget's 1px full-height left BORDER and the Cloudflare LOGO; restrict to the left 30%. FINALLY: repeated fresh-profile attempts from the same PIIP get served the SPINNER-ONLY variant that no click can clear - stop and retry later or change region rather than hammering.
